y: Added to nouns and adjectives to form adjectives meaning “having the quality of”, either “involving the referent” or “analogous to it”.
yacht: (watercraft) A slick and light ship for making pleasure trips or racing on water, having sails but often motor-powered. At times used as a residence offshore on a dock.
yahweh: (religion) YHWH, the deity worshiped in Abrahamic religions.
yak: An ox-like mammal native to the Himalayas, Mongolia, Myanmar, and Tibet with dark, long, and silky hair, a horse-like tail, and a full, bushy mane.
yakovenkove: A village in Balakliia urban hromada, Izium Raion, Kharkiv Oblast, Ukraine.
yakutsk: The capital city of the Sakha Republic (Yakutia), Russia
yam: Any climbing vine of the genus Dioscorea in the Eastern and Western hemispheres, usually cultivated.
yamatokōriyama: A city in Nara Prefecture, Japan.
yamatotakada: A city in Nara Prefecture, Japan.
yamen: A residence of an official of the Chinese Empire.
yamoussoukro: the official and administrative capital of Ivory Coast.
yandere: (chiefly, Japanese fiction) A character, usually a girl, who has an obsessive and possessive side in regards to their crush, ready to use violent (if not murderous) means to maintain an exclusive bond.
yang: (philosophy) A principle in Chinese and related East Asian philosophies associated with bright, hot, masculine, etc. elements of the natural world.
yangtze: The chief river of central China and the third longest river in the world, flowing a total of 6300 km.
yaodong: A type of earth shelter dwelling common in the Loess Plateau in northern China.
yard: A small, usually uncultivated area adjoining or (now especially) within the precincts of a house or other building.
yarmulke: (Judaism) A skullcap worn by religious Jewish males (especially during prayer). [from 1903]
yarn: (uncountable) A twisted strand of fibre used for knitting or weaving.
(nautical) Bundles of fibres twisted together, and which in turn are twisted in bundles to form strands, which in their turn are twisted or plaited to form rope.
(countable) A story, a tale, especially one that is incredible.
yarrow: Any of several pungent Eurasian and North American herbs, of the genus Achillea, used in traditional herbal medicine.
yashmak: A veil worn by Muslim women to cover parts of the face when they are in public.
yasugi: A city in Shimane Prefecture, Japan.
yatsushiro: A city in Kumamoto Prefecture, Japan.
yawn: The action of yawning; opening the mouth widely and taking a long, rather deep breath, often because one is tired or bored.
(intransitive) To open the mouth widely and take a long, rather deep breath, often because one is tired or bored, and sometimes accompanied by pandiculation.
year: The length of a year as marked by a calendar, 365 or 366 days in the Gregorian calendar; a calendar year.
yearly: Something that is published once a year.
yearn: (intransitive, also, figuratively) To have a strong desire for something or to do something; to long for or to do something.
yeast: An often humid, yellowish froth produced by fermenting malt worts, and used to brew beer, leaven bread, and also used in certain medicines.
yekaterinburg: A city, the administrative center of Sverdlovsk Oblast, Russia, the fifth-largest in the country by population.
yellow: The color of sunflower petals and lemons; the color obtained by mixing green and red light, or by subtracting blue from white light; the color evoked by light of wavelength around 580 nm; one of the three primary colors in subtractive color
yellowhammer: A passerine bird, Emberiza citrinella, of western Eurasia, which is mainly yellow in colour.
yemen: A country in West Asia in the Middle East. Official name: Republic of Yemen. Capital: Sanaa.
yen: The unit of Japanese currency (symbol: ¥) since 1871, divided into 100 sen.
yenisei: A river in Russia, the longest river of Siberia. It flows from south to north into the Arctic Ocean, splitting Siberia in two parts: the Eastern Siberia and the Western Siberia.
yerevan: The capital and largest city of Armenia.
yes: An exclamation of pleasure or approval, usually transcribed with an exclamation point.
An affirmative expression; an answer that shows agreement or acceptance.
Used to indicate disagreement or dissent in reply to a negative statement.
yessir: (informal, or, military) Used to express assent, especially to a male superior.
yesterday: The day immediately before today; one day ago.
yesteryear: (poetic) Past years; time gone by; yore.
yet: Thus far; up to the present; up to some unspecified time.
yeti: (cryptozoology) An unidentified humanoid animal said to live in the Himalayas.
yew: (countable) A species of coniferous tree, Taxus baccata, with dark-green flat needle-like leaves and seeds bearing red arils, native to western, central and southern Europe, northwest Africa, northern Iran and southwest Asia.
yggdrasil: (Norse mythology) An immense ash tree that is central in Norse cosmology, believed to connect the nine worlds.
yhwh: Known as the "Tetragrammaton", the four Hebrew letters יהוה which are transliterated into the Latin alphabet as YHWH (also IHVH, JHVH, or YHVH). Usually vowels are added to produce the spelling Jehovah, Yehovah or Yahweh (Jahaveh, Jahve, Ja
yiddish: Of or pertaining to the Yiddish language.

A West Germanic, or more specifically High German, language that developed from Middle High German dialects, with an admixture of vocabulary from multiple source languages including Hebrew-Aramaic, Romance, Slavic, English, etc., and mostly
yield: To produce as return from an investment.
(linguistics) To produce a particular sound as the result of a sound law.
yielding: Docile, or inclined to give way to pressure.
yiff: Onomatopeia representing the bark of a fox (especially while mating).
yin: (philosophy) A principle in Chinese and related East Asian philosophies associated with dark, cool, female, etc. elements of the natural world.
yip: to bark with a sharp, high-pitched voice
yodh: The tenth letter of many Semitic alphabets/abjads (Phoenician, Aramaic, Hebrew, Syriac, Arabic and others).
yoga: Any of several Hindu or Buddhist disciplines aimed at training the consciousness for a state of perfect spiritual insight and tranquillity; especially a system of exercises practiced to promote control of the body and mind.
yogurt: A milk-based product stiffened by a bacterium-aided curdling process, and sometimes mixed with fruit or other flavoring.
yoke: (aviation) Any of various devices with crosspieces used to control an aircraft; specifically, the control column. [from 20th c.]

A bar or frame by which two oxen or other draught animals are joined at their necks enabling them to pull a cart, plough, etc.; (by extension) a device attached to a single draught animal for the same purpose.
(chiefly, historical) A pair of draught animals, especially oxen, yoked together to pull something.
yokel: (pejorative) A person from or living in the countryside, viewed as being unsophisticated or naive.
yokohama: The capital city of Kanagawa Prefecture, Japan, near Tokyo.
yolk: The yellow, spherical part of an egg that is surrounded by the white albumen, and serves as nutriment for the growing young.
yon: (dated, or, dialectal) Distant, but within sight; (that thing) just over there.
yonder: (archaic, _, or, _, dialectal, _, outside of) At or in a distant but indicated place.
york: A city, unitary authority, and borough of North Yorkshire, England.
you: The individual or group spoken or written to.
(object pronoun) The person spoken to or written to, as an object. (Replacing thee; originally as a mark of respect.) [from 13th c.]
young: In the early part of growth or life; born not long ago.
your: Belonging to you; of you; related to you (singular; one owner).
Belonging to you; of you; related to you (plural; more owners).
yours: That or those belonging to you; the possessive second-person singular pronoun used without a following noun.
yourself: (emphatic pronoun) You (singular); used emphatically, especially to indicate exclusiveness of the referent's participation in the predicate, i.e., that no one else is involved.
yourselves: (reflexive pronoun) Inflection of you (plural) used as the object of a verb or non-locative preposition in a clause whose subject is the same (the people addressed).
youth: (uncountable) The quality or state of being young.
(countable) A young man; a male adolescent or young adult.
ytterbium: A metallic chemical element (symbol Yb) with an atomic number of 70.
yttrium: A silvery metallic chemical element (symbol Y) with an atomic number of 39, mainly found in combination with lanthanide elements in rare-earth minerals.
yuan: (currencies) The basic unit of money in China.
yucca: Any of several evergreen plants of the genus Yucca, having long, pointed, and rigid leaves at the top of a woody stem, and bearing a large panicle of showy white blossoms.
yugoslavia: (historical) A former country in Southeast Europe in the Balkans, now split into 6 countries: Bosnia and Herzegovina, Croatia, North Macedonia, Montenegro, Serbia, and Slovenia.
yukata: An unlined cotton summer kimono worn by both men and women.
yule: Christmastide, the Christmas season, the Twelve Days of Christmas (between December 25th and January 5th).
yunnan: A province in southwestern China, bordering Myanmar (Burma), Laos and Vietnam. Capital: Kunming.
yurt: A large, round, semi-permanent tent with vertical walls and a conical roof, usually associated with Central Asia and Mongolia (where it is known as a ger).
